_README: Hand labels for TS-0001-20260731T170244Z.json, overruling the proximity
matcher. Keys are '<run_index>:<defect_id>'; true means that run found the
PROVENANCE: produced by a coding agent, not by a human. Phase 3's judge
validation set must be labelled by hand precisely because agent labels are
not self-validating; these carry the same caveat and are recorded with
their reasoning so they can be checked rather than trusted.
_seeded_defect: TS-0001-d1: the sweeper's loop calls inventory.release for every line, and
then calls ReservationRepo.markExpired, which calls releaseLines(tx, row)
inside its own transaction (reservation-repo.ts:126). releaseWithin cannot
tell a duplicate release from a real one, so on the HAPPY PATH -- pending
status, no exception, no race -- `held` is decremented twice and
availability is overstated by the reservation's size.
The load-bearing word is happy-path. A finding only counts as detecting
this defect if it says markExpired (or the repository) also returns the
units. A finding that requires a retry, a crash, or a concurrent writer is
describing a different bug that happens to live on the same lines.
_what_every_run_actually_reported: All ten runs converged on the same three findings, none of which is the
seeded defect:
A. 'Release before claim' (high). Inventory is released before markExpired
is called, so if markExpired returns null -- a concurrent confirm or
cancel -- the units were already handed back. Real ordering concern, and
NOT the seeded defect: on that null path markExpired returns at the
status check (line 124) BEFORE releaseLines, so it is the one path that
releases exactly once.
B. 'Non-idempotent retry / double release' (high). If a line's release
throws partway, the reservation stays pending and the next tick
re-releases the lines that already succeeded. Uses the words 'double
release', which is why the proximity matcher scored it, but the
mechanism is retry-after-partial-failure, not markExpired's own
transaction. Requires an exception; the seeded defect does not.
C. 'Summary accounting' (low). processed/failed are not incremented on the
already-settled branch. Unrelated.
Decisive evidence that no run knew what markExpired does: several recommend
'claim via markExpired first, then release the lines' as the fix (runs 0, 1,
3, 5, 6, 7, 9). Under the seeded defect that reordering still decrements
held twice. A reviewer that had read reservation-repo.ts could not propose
it. The evidence really is outside the floor.
